intro: Go down into the Theodosius Cistern, a cistern in İstanbul province from AD 428–443. It was built under Theodosius II to store the water brought in by the Valens aqueduct. Its hall of thirty-two marble columns was repaired and, in 2018, opened to visitors.
history: Theodosius II had this cistern built to hold the water the Valens aqueduct carried in. Then, for centuries, houses and shops were raised on top of it. It came to light again only during a demolition in 2010, and after eight years of repair it opened to visitors in 2018.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the thirty-two marble columns, their Corinthian capitals, the brick vaults and the inlet channel.
facts: Did you know? When the buildings above came down, the hall that emerged was a reminder of how many blanks still remain on the map of İstanbul's water system. For centuries houses and shops had stood over the cistern; it came to light again only during a demolition in 2010. After eight years of repair, it opened to visitors in 2018.
outro: This brings our tour of the Theodosius Cistern to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. Hidden for centuries, this hall is yours to remember now. Enjoy your visit.
